name: Coleman Farthing
summary: In Brill's Gallows' End Tavern, Coleman Farthing nurses a hatred born in the Agamand Mills. He served the wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal, where he and the other laborers died defending their employers' estate from the Scourge. Now Forsaken, he seeks vengeance on his former masters.

sections.title: A Bitter Servant
sections.body: Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing worked at the Agamand Mills, Tirisfal Glades' largest milling and agricultural operation. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. They urged their household and laborers to take up arms, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters. Every last one of them died.

sections.title: Vengeance from the Grave
sections.body: Coleman Farthing broke free into the Forsaken after being raised into undeath, and he still hates the Agamands. He blames his former employers' greed and pride for tricking their staff into an impossible last stand, not only the Scourge. From a tavern in Brill, he sends Horde champions to the blighted mills to kill the risen Agamand kin and plunder heirloom weapons from their family crypt, stripping away the last of their honor.

faq.q: Where can Coleman Farthing be found?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing spends his days in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, in central Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Why does Coleman hate the Agamand family so much?
faq.answer: When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the Agamand patriarchs persuaded their workers, Coleman among them, to stay and defend the mills instead of fleeing. The entire workforce was slaughtered, and Coleman sees their call to fight as arrogant manipulation that led him to his death.

faq.q: What happened to the Agamand Mills?
faq.answer: The Scourge overran the sprawling estate. Its wind-driven mills lie ruined and haunted, while Agamand family members and their slain workers wander the blighted fields as mindlessly hostile undead under the Lich King's sway.

faq.q: What tasks does Coleman give to adventurers?
faq.answer: Coleman sends adventurers north to the Agamand Mills to cull the roaming undead, slay risen members of the Agamand lineage and recover their remains for desecration, then plunder ancestral weapons from the Agamand Family Crypt.

faq.q: Why does Coleman want the Agamand heirloom weapons?
faq.answer: Coleman sees the Agamands' ancestral weapons as signs of the hollow pride that led his fellow workers to die. He sends warriors to plunder them from the family crypt, stripping the dynasty of its honor and putting the weapons to practical use against their enemies.

faq.q: Is Coleman Farthing related to Bishop Farthing?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing and Bishop Farthing share a surname and roots in the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, but no confirmed record establishes their family ties.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, Coleman reflects the resentment many commoners hold toward Lordaeron's old nobility, whose arrogance and pride often hastened their subjects' deaths during the plague.
Coleman points aspiring warriors toward the Agamand Family Crypt to plunder the martial heirlooms of a fallen aristocratic house and arm themselves for the wars ahead.
